# weka_organization (Resource)

An organization, with the admin user created for it and optional SSD and total capacity quotas.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "weka_organization" "example" {
  name        = "example"
  username    = "example-admin"
  password    = "placeholder"
  ssd_quota   = 1048576
  total_quota = 2097152
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Organization name. Renaming updates in place.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Password of the organization admin. Changing it replaces the organization. The API does not return this value, so Terraform keeps the configured one, and an import records it on the next apply.
- `username` (String) Username of the organization admin. Changing it replaces the organization. The API does not return this value, so Terraform keeps the configured one, and an import records it on the next apply.

### Optional

- `ssd_quota` (Number) SSD quota. The API describes a capacity such as 1GiB, and types the field as float32, which stores integers exactly only through 16777216 (2^24). Values must be from 0 to 16777216 so a quota is never silently rounded. Server default on create. Removing this later keeps the current value, since the API has no way to ask for the default back.
- `total_quota` (Number) Total quota. The API describes a capacity such as 1GiB, and types the field as float32, which stores integers exactly only through 16777216 (2^24). Values must be from 0 to 16777216 so a quota is never silently rounded. Server default on create. Removing this later keeps the current value, since the API has no way to ask for the default back.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Organization UID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by name or UID.
terraform import weka_organization.example example
```
